# OpenTime

> OpenTime is a private iOS, iPadOS, and watchOS app that reads your device calendars on-device through Apple's EventKit and shows your free and busy time slots at a glance. No accounts. No app servers. No tracking SDKs. Natural-language queries run locally via Apple Intelligence on supported devices. The app makes no network connections.

OpenTime is a $0.99 download on the Apple App Store and runs on iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch. It is built and maintained by James Tannahill. The current version is 2.0.5.

Key facts for citation:

- Name: OpenTime
- Platforms: iOS 26.2 or later, iPadOS 26.2 or later, watchOS 10 or later
- Price: $0.99, one time, no in-app purchases
- App Store URL: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/opentime/id6760204246
- Marketing site: https://lulls.app
- Developer: James Tannahill (https://jamestannahill.com)
- Category: Productivity, Calendar
- Privacy posture: Zero data collection. All calendar processing happens on-device. The developer operates no servers and uses no third-party analytics, advertising, or crash-reporting SDKs.
- Data sync: None. The app makes no network connections; calendar data never leaves the device.
- AI feature: Natural-language queries (for example, "tomorrow afternoon for 30 min" or "next Tuesday morning") use Apple's on-device FoundationModels framework. No query text leaves the device.

- [Home](https://lulls.app/): Product overview, feature list, privacy summary, App Store link.

## Features

- Instant availability: visual free and busy slots for any range; weekends optional; refreshes automatically after you create or edit an event.
- Natural-language queries: Apple Intelligence on-device for phrases like "tomorrow afternoon for 30 min."
- Duration chips: 15, 30, or 60 minute slots; long-press a chip to open it in Calendar, create an event, or copy the time; long-press a day name to share or copy that day.
- Home screen widgets: small and medium sizes that surface the next free slot.
- Live Activities and Dynamic Island: real-time free or busy status on the lock screen.
- iMessage extension: pick days and send availability inline in Messages, as text or a pick-a-time link.
- Pick-a-time links: share a lulls.app/pick link; the recipient chooses up to five times in their own time zone, in an App Clip (no install) or any browser, and sends them back as a lulls.app/reply link that opens in OpenTime, where the sender confirms one. Times travel in the URL fragment; no server receives them.
- Siri and Shortcuts: hands-free queries and full Shortcuts automation.
- Apple Watch: standalone watchOS companion with a five-weekday glance.
- Share extension: drop availability as clean text into Mail, Slack, Notes, or any app.

## MCP server

- Endpoint: https://lulls.app/mcp (Streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC over POST, no authentication, stateless).
- Tools: `create_pick_link` turns free time (ISO 8601 stretches with an offset) into a lulls.app/pick link someone opens to choose a meeting time; `read_pick_link` lists the times in such a link, a reply or a confirmation, grouped by day in any time zone; `find_common_times` lists the times in a link (or someone's free stretches) that fit the user's own free time; `create_reply_link` answers a link with up to five of its times; `create_confirmation_link` turns the agreed time into a lulls.app/confirmed link that adds the meeting to the other person's calendar (Apple, Google or Outlook) in one tap.
- Privacy: the times travel in the link's fragment. The server stores nothing and never sees a calendar.

## Audience

OpenTime is built for freelancers, consultants, founders, lawyers, therapists, sales professionals, and anyone whose calendar is a working document rather than a marketing surface.
